source.title: Long-Term Trazodone Use and Cognition: A Potential Therapeutic Role for Slow-Wave Sleep Enhancers

confidence_rationale: Directly and almost uniquely addressed to IMPL-026's boldest assertion -- that a slow-wave-sleep enhancer carries disease-progression-modifying potential -- and the effect reported is large (2.6-fold slower MMSE decline). But n = 25 versus 25, retrospective, single-centre, and with no polysomnography at all, so the slow-wave mechanism in the title is inferred rather than measured. Held near the boundary of the moderate band for that reason.
failure_signatures: No polysomnography was performed, so the paper's own titular mechanism -- slow-wave sleep enhancement -- is never observed; the benefit tracked subjective sleep improvement instead.
n = 25 trazodone users versus 25 propensity-matched non-users at a single centre: an effect this large in a sample this small is a candidate for regression to the mean on replication.
Retrospective and non-randomised, so indication and adherence differences between users and non-users remain plausible alternative explanations for the cognitive difference.
The authors themselves decline to claim causation and state that prospective confirmation is required to establish whether any effect operates through slow-wave sleep enhancement.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In 25 trazodone users versus 25 propensity-matched non-users followed about four years, non-users declined 2.6-fold faster on MMSE -- 0.70 (95% CI 0.50-0.90) versus 0.27 (95% CI 0.07-0.48) points per year (p = 0.023) -- with benefit especially associated with subjective improvement of sleep complaints in post-hoc analysis (p = 0.0006).
mapping.ree_translation: IMPL-026 places trazodone (25-100 mg) in the architecture-preserving tier with 'Risk: IMPROVES Phase 1/2 fidelity. DPM potential: YES'. This is the primary human evidence behind that DPM assignment, and it is consistent with the REE reading that protecting Phase 1/2 consolidation protects downstream schema integrity rather than merely improving sleep comfort.
mapping.mapping_caveat: IMPL-026 classifies medications by PREDICTED phase-specific pipeline disruption (INV-045 Phase 0-4). This paper measures neither phase-resolved consolidation nor any REE pipeline quantity; the mapping runs from a clinical endpoint back to a mechanism the study did not observe. The specific hazard here is that the study is cited for a slow-wave mechanism it did not measure: the mediator actually associated with benefit was SUBJECTIVE sleep improvement, which is compatible with, but does not establish, Phase 1/2 enhancement. Treating this entry as confirmation of the phase mechanism would be circular.
mapping.source_context: Human retrospective cohort, memory-clinic population, approximately 4-year follow-up, MMSE endpoint.

confidence_components.notes: Unusually, mapping_fidelity exceeds source_quality here: the paper is aimed squarely at IMPL-026's question but is methodologically thin. The aggregate is pulled below the mean of the components because for a disease-modification claim the design weakness is the dominant consideration, not the topical match.
